    Run Embedded Standard Setting Analysis

    emstans.Rd

    `emstans()` estimates cut scores with Embedded Standard Setting (ESS) from panelists' item-level alignments and item locations. Each grade and round is analysed separately: cut scores are estimated for every panelist and for the modal alignment across panelists (per table and for all tables), and the median and average of the panelist cuts are reported. For the modal result of each grade, the function also reports agreement between aligned and empirical levels, an item review, and impact data.

    Usage

    emstans(
  file = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  ...,
  grades = NULL,
  location = "RP67",
  method = c("weight", "count"),
  smooth = FALSE,
  by_domain = FALSE,
  domains = NULL,
  font_size = 14,
  digits = 3
)

    Arguments

    file

    Path to an emss Excel workbook (sheets Setup, Panelists, Ratings, ItemMetaData, ExamineeMetaData). Either `file` or `data` must be given.

    data

    An object from [ess_data()] or [ess_read_excel()], or a list of data frames in the workbook's sheet order (setup, panelists, ratings, item data, examinee data).

    ...

    Former argument names, still accepted with a warning. All arguments after `data` must be named in full. Former names: `filePath` (now `file`), `grade` (`grades`), `loc` (`location`), `WESS` (`method`), `gamest` (`smooth`), `domain` and `select_domain` (`by_domain`, `domains`), `targets` (use the `columns` argument of [ess_data()]) and `median` (no longer needed: modal, median and average cuts are always reported).

    grades

    Grades to analyse: `NULL` for all, a numeric vector of positions, or a character vector of grade names. Default `NULL`.

    location

    Name of the item location column, such as `"RP67"` or `"RP50"`. Default `"RP67"`.

    method

    `"weight"` for ESS-Weight (minimise the summed distance of inconsistent items) or `"count"` for ESS-Count (minimise their number). Default `"weight"`.

    smooth

    If `TRUE`, cut scores are the minima of a GAM-smoothed inconsistency profile instead of the exact minima. Default `FALSE`.

    by_domain

    If `TRUE`, each content domain (the item data's Domain column) is also analysed separately, in addition to all items of each grade. Default `FALSE`.

    domains

    With `by_domain = TRUE`, the domains to analyse; `NULL` for all of them.

    font_size

    Font size for plots. Default `14`.

    digits

    Decimal places in printed tables. Default `3`.

    Value

    An object of class `"ESS"`. Use [extract()] to get its tables, [report()] for an HTML report, [plot()] for plots, [update()] to set cut scores manually and [bootstrapping()] for bootstrap cut scores.

    Examples

    if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
res <- emstans("study.xlsx", location = "RP67")
res
extract(res, "cutscore")
report(res)

# ESS-Count, and each content domain separately
emstans("study.xlsx", method = "count", by_domain = TRUE)

# CSV input with custom column names and level labels
d <- ess_data(ratings = "ratings.csv", items = "items.csv",
              levels = c("Basic", "Intermediate", "Advanced"))
res <- emstans(data = d, location = "RP50")
} # }
